out-of-order reassembly queue (future segments are discarded with duplicate ACK)

DATA-SEQ.interpretation: Each new data octet consumes one sequence number; cumulative ACK removes an acknowledged prefix. Retransmission does not advance SND.NXT.

DATA-ACK.interpretation: New ACKs satisfy SND.UNA < SEG.ACK <= SND.NXT; duplicate and old ACKs do not remove data; future ACK triggers an ACK.

DATA-WINDOW.interpretation: Update SND.WND only for acceptable ACK and newer WL1/WL2. Segmentation respects the available advertised send window.

DATA-RECEIVE.interpretation: Accept and trim text overlapping the receive window; advance RCV.NXT only over contiguous newly accepted bytes, ACK the next expected octet.

DATA-SEND.interpretation: Model buffers application octets and segments them within the configured capacity, MSS and send window.

DATA-RTX.interpretation: The retransmission timer sends the oldest outstanding data again. This profile uses fixed initial RTO and exponential backoff only.

DATA-RTO.interpretation: Start on first outstanding transmission, restart on new partial ACK, cancel on all acknowledged, retransmit oldest on expiry and double RTO (5.1-5.6). No RTT sampling or maximum retry policy.

DATA-SCOPE.interpretation: Finite single-connection profile, 16-byte send and receive capacity, MSS=4, handshake-advertised peer window, immediate ACK and explicit flush scheduler. Future/out-of-order data discarded without reassembly. Close requires buffers drained. No implementation conformance claim.

CONNECTION-PROFILE.interpretation: Inherited single-connection control paths retain validated control shapes, exact sequence checks and configurable user/MSL deadlines. The data extension supersedes the base zero-payload assumption only in ESTABLISHED, within the explicit DATA-SCOPE boundary; data in other lifecycle states remains excluded.
